3.17    S17: Critical determinant bounds restricted to actual adjoint maximizers
Status: unresolved question in the manuscript.
Full problem description. When v− (h) = 0, determine whether the critical Ln/(n−1) estimate
can hold for the determinant-weighted probabilities of exact maximizing currents representing ad-
joints, uniformly as F ranges over a speciﬁed bounded set. Identify geometric or density hypotheses
for such a restricted estimate.
State of the art. All normalized Gauduchon tests can violate the endpoint, while their subcrit-
ical estimates hold universally. Adjoint densities inherit those subcritical bounds; positive lower
mass supplies the endpoint. For one ﬁxed smooth strictly positive density the exact maximizer
is smooth and unique. Near-maximizing sequences can have divergent higher moments even on
Kähler manifolds.
Remaining gap. The failure for the full test family does not decide estimates for exact maximizers.
Conversely, boundedness for one smooth datum is not uniformity over a family. State precisely
whether the estimated object is kT or the normalized F -weighted density. This may aid P16 but
does not itself prove singleton supports.

author/chapter_research_program.tex:146.

unchanged_original_condition_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n>=3, h a smooth positive Hermitian form, and dV a smooth positive probability volume. Suppose the bounded-potential lower Monge-Ampere mass v_-(h) is zero. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. Let G_h be the positive (n-1,n-1)-currents T with dd^c T=0 and integral h wedge T=1. In an h-unitary frame, write sigma_T=h wedge T and the positive Hermitian matrix density P_T characterized by beta wedge T=(1/n)tr(B P_T)d sigma_T, tr P_T=n, where B is the matrix of a smooth (1,1)-form beta relative to h. For a real continuous logarithmic density F, set Gamma_F(T)=(exp(F)dV/h^n)^(1/n) det(P_T)^(1/n) sigma_T and D_F(T)=Gamma_F(T)(X). The attained maximum M(F)>0 equals exp(-B_0(F)/n), where B_0(F) is the scalar in MA_h(u)=exp(B_0(F)+F)dV. For every exact maximizing current T, the determinant-weighted probability nu_(T,F)=Gamma_F(T)/M(F) is absolutely continuous with respect to dV and represents an adjoint/supporting probability of B_0. If F is smooth, the exact maximizing current is unique, smooth and strictly positive: it is the normalized (n-1)st power of the Gauduchon form conformal to the smooth solution form. In the smooth case Gamma_F(T)=exp(F/n)k_T dV with k_T=(gamma^n/dV)^((n-1)/n) for T=gamma^(n-1), respecting trace normalization. At an actual maximizer one can equivalently define its determinant density by k_T=exp(-F/n)M(F)d nu_(T,F)/dV.

Original S17 asks whether a uniform critical L^(n/(n-1)) estimate can hold for the determinant-weighted probabilities of exact maximizing currents representing adjoints, uniformly as F ranges over a specified bounded set, when v_-(h)=0. Identify geometric or density hypotheses giving such a restricted estimate. Specify the bounded family, its topology/quantitative bounds, whether all its data are smooth or continuous, and whether the estimated density is k_T or d nu_(T,F)/dV. The endpoint can fail for the full normalized Gauduchon test family, whereas every strictly smaller exponent has a universal estimate. Positive lower mass gives the full endpoint, but is excluded here. One fixed smooth strictly positive density has a unique smooth maximizer; this fact is background and is not a uniform theorem over a family. Near-maximizing sequences can have divergent higher moments even on Kahler manifolds. Distinguish exact maximizers from all tests and from near-maximizers. No candidate density family, geometric condition, estimate or proof is supplied.
unchanged_original_condition_task.completionCriteria: Prove new explicit sufficient geometric or density conditions giving an actual uniform critical estimate over a nontrivial specified bounded family at zero lower mass, or construct an actual compact-complex counterexample family of exact adjoint maximizers with rigorously proved endpoint failure. Expand the quantitative family assumptions and demonstrate they are nonvacuous in the stated zero-lower-mass setting. A single datum, finite list, mere constant shifts, the known full-family failure, or a statement about near-maximizers does not solve the uniform exact-maximizer problem. Check all indispensable external hypotheses against primary sources and independently reconstruct the full proof. Clearly retain the boundary between the proved restricted result and any unresolved broader family; do not claim P16 singleton supports from an endpoint estimate alone.

primary_application_assessment: Reuse the historically root-assessed exact elliptic primary proofs for unchanged hypotheses. The current article explicitly reconstructs the Sobolev-to-full-Holder Fredholm passage without assuming smooth density in Holder norm, the maximum/minimum principle with the correct zeroth-order sign, and weak adjoint/supporting identities. Compactness, smooth uniform ellipticity and positivity are checked for each operator; probability and trace normalizations are independently recalculated. No new mathematical application or new unreviewed theorem is introduced by this scope assessment.

clause_assessment.requested: Uniform critical estimate over a specified bounded family when lower mass is zero
clause_assessment.proved: The explicit positive-radius smooth C2alpha probability ball has uniform Linfinity bounds for every exact maximizer; hence criticalLq bounds. The radius contains no lower-mass term.

clause_assessment.requested: Geometric or density hypotheses and nontriviality
clause_assessment.proved: The theorem chooses quantitative strong-topology density smallness; the normalized family is infinite dimensional on every fixed zero-mass background and contains distinct data with distinct exact maximizing currents.
Probability density qF and trace-normalized determinant density kTF have separate exact formulas and separately proved uniform constants.

clause_assessment.requested: Distinguish exact maximizers from full tests and near-maximizers
clause_assessment.proved: AMGM and Stokes prove exact global maximality over all currents; equality plus scalar elliptic regularity identifies every exact maximizer. No unrestricted test bound is asserted.

clause_assessment.requested: Do not infer P16 singleton supports
clause_assessment.proved: Local smooth current uniqueness is proved from equality and ellipticity; no general continuous-density P16 assertion is made.

scope_assessment: The original asks whether the estimate can hold on a specified bounded set and requests hypotheses. The infinite-dimensional explicitly bounded smooth family answers every requested clause. A universal theorem for all continuous bounded families was not requested and remains open. This corrects catalogue accounting, without broadening the proved theorem.
